rationale: THE CONSTRUCTOR-RECEIVER OWNER (C9, 2026-11-25). `new Worker().run()` states the receiver's class outright in the `new_expression` field `constructor`, but receiverOwnerType had branches only for identifier / subscript_expression / member_expression, so this shape carried NO `metadata.owner`. The store then fell back to the NAME model and bound `run` to whichever same-named member won its tie-break. MEASURED on a three-file repro (used.ts declares `Worker.run`, other.ts declares `Other.run`, main.ts calls `new Worker().run()` and imports only Worker): bb bound the call to `other.ts:run`, i.e. a call to a class the file never imports. The rival class `Other` is load-bearing — without a same-named member in the file the name model resolves correctly and this fixture passes with or without the fix. The control row (`viaLocal`) pins that the branch does not steal a row the annotation class already owns.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAIN: the owner is the constructor's own name — the class the source wrote, not a name-model guess
CONTROL: the annotated-local path keeps its own evidence class; C9 must not reclassify it

expectRelationshipCount.note: exactly one call row — a fix that also emitted a constructor call from the same site would fail here

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT: binding the call to the rival class the file never imports
THE PRE-FIX SHAPE: the owner channel silent, leaving the store to the name model
